designs.title: Summit Ridge
designs.why: Two masses that don't connect: a sparse, broken-line far range on top and a dense ridge below, with a dead band of white between them. The only type is a tiny unnamed '6,861 m' in the corner, so nothing anchors the piece. From 3 m it reads as scattered marks.
designs.fix: Close the gap so the ridge carries the eye up to the summit, and set a proper caption block (peak name plus height) under the drawing in place of the orphaned corner label.

designs.title: Kitesurfing
designs.why: The diagonal from kite to rider has real energy, and the rider and spray are well drawn. But the middle is mostly empty line-space, and the widely tracked thin sans caption is tiny and stylistically apart from the drawing, so it disappears on the tee.
designs.fix: Make the KITESURFING caption bigger and heavier (about twice the cap height, tracking cut by half) and centre it under the board's spray line so it locks to the figure.

designs.title: Coral
designs.why: A classic plate with a clear main specimen, a secondary colony and detail studies that balance it. 'CORAL.' in spaced roman caps with the period is well judged. Small screen-dot moiré patches show up in the branch shading.
designs.fix: Replace the crosshatch dither patches in the main branch with line or stipple so the texture matches the rest and prints cleanly.

designs.title: Antarctica
designs.why: The family group makes a readable, symmetrical cluster that works from a distance. The heavy geometric sans heading with its rule clashes with the engraved drawing, and the ink stops dead on a flat baseline with no ground, so the bottom feels cut off.
designs.fix: Set ANTARCTICA in a spaced roman serif that matches the engraving, and add a light ice-line or shadow under the feet to seat the group.

designs.title: Bait Ball
designs.why: The strongest pure graphic of the set. The spiral reads instantly from 3 m, the density gradient from the dense core to scattered outer fish is beautifully paced, and with no type there is nothing to go wrong.
designs.fix: Tighten the few stray outer fish at the lower left so the silhouette's edge is a deliberate taper rather than a random scatter.

designs.title: Beluga
designs.why: The diagonal pose fills the format well, but the body is almost all bare outline, so on the tee it reads as a thin line drawing with little presence. The caption type is blobby and degraded, and the second line 'RANGE: ARCTIC OCEAN' is heavier than the title, which inverts the hierarchy.
designs.fix: Reset the caption cleanly: BELUGA as the dominant line, and RANGE: ARCTIC OCEAN smaller, in a lighter weight and crisply rendered (no blotched letterforms).

designs.title: Humpback Whale
designs.why: A well-organised plate with fine engraving and a sensible three-tier layout. The title is redundant ('WHALE' over 'Humpback Whale'), and a dozen small labels make it fussy and illegible from 3 m. Some labels, such as 'Fluke (ventral view)', float without a leader.
designs.fix: Drop the redundant 'WHALE' line, cut the labels to the five or six essential ones and give each a leader.

designs.title: Octopus
designs.why: Excellent radial composition: the arms curl out to fill the rectangle, the silhouette is strong and the caption pairs roman caps with an italic binomial in a textbook way. The only flaw is screen-dot dither patches in the eyes and mantle shading.
designs.fix: Redraw the dithered patches around the eyes as line hatching so they don't moiré or fill in on the print.

designs.title: Patagonia
designs.why: A pleasant panorama, but the line is thin and open, so it goes faint on the tee. The peak labels are set in a crude, blotchy bitmap-looking serif with commas that render as dots ('3.405'). Five labels plus coordinates crowd the type.
designs.fix: Re-set all the labels in a clean serif with correct thousands commas, at one consistent size, and drop the label count to the three main peaks.

designs.title: El Calafate
designs.why: A strong typographic object with a clear focal arm (EL CALAFATE 0 km) and an even rhythm of condensed caps down the post. It reads well from 3 m. Wood-grain dashes sit right on the type baseline between name and distance and look like stray underscores.
designs.fix: Clear the wood-grain strokes from the text line on each arm so names and distances sit on clean board.

designs.title: Ushuaia
designs.why: Composed as a confident vignette: peaks, town and reflected water build a solid rectangle, and the spaced roman title with small coordinates below is well proportioned. Most finished-looking piece here.
designs.fix: Shorten the coordinates to two decimals (54.80° S 68.30° W) so the line is quieter and matches the title width better.

designs.title: Belize
designs.why: Nice scene and a well-set title, but three stacked zones (scene, chart with compass, title) compete. The sparse chart with floating sounding numbers reads as noise from a distance.
designs.fix: Shrink or simplify the chart zone (fewer soundings, a tighter reef outline) so the caye scene clearly dominates and the chart becomes a quiet secondary band.
